title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol, will start Week 3
items.desc: Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.impact: Murray missed the Vikings Week 2 slog of a win over the Bears, but he will be back in the lineup for Week 3 against a hapless Tampa defense. Murray is still a bit of an unknown at this point given he barely played in Week 1, but this is a perfect matchup to return to.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Chad Ryland quiet in loss to Seattle
items.desc: Chad Ryland hit his only PAT in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.impact: It was a quiet day for the Cardinals kicker, who didn't even get to attempt a field goal the whole game. Better days will come for him, but he's tough to trust for fantasy.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Arizona Cardinals D/ST run over by Seattle offense in Week 2
items.desc: The Arizona Cardinals D/ST was completely outmatched against the Seattle Seahawks offensive attack, losing 34-3 in the process. The unit managed just one sack and a fumble recovery.
items.impact: After a half-decent showing against the Chargers, the Cardinals defense was put back in their place by the much better run Seattle offense. Arizona's lack of talent on the defensive side of the ball screams that they should be well off of streaming radar, and that was evident on Sunday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle sprain) to undergo surgery, out indefinitely
items.desc: Saints OT Kelvin Banks Jr. suffered a severe high-ankle sprain and is now expected to have surgery to repair it.
items.impact: Banks will be sidelined indefinitely. He has a chance to return late in the season if all goes well.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Emmett Johnson expected to continue to see more snaps
items.desc: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson will continue to get more and more snaps.
items.impact: Reid added that Johnson will see more snaps and take some of the workload off of Kenneth Walker. The rookie has flashed in a limited role over the first two weeks of the season. He remains a solid stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Patrick Jones II (back) hopeful to return in Week 3
items.desc: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he optimistic about LB Pat Jones potentially returning this week at Cleveland.
items.impact: Jones missed the first two games of the season with a back injury.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Josh Simmons (back) without clear update on return
items.desc: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said the team anticipated Josh Simmons would miss "two, three, four games."
items.impact: Reid said Simmons has been doing 'everything' behind the scenes. The Chiefs want to make sure his swelling is down.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) trending in right direction
items.desc: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Mansoor Delane could have played if needed on Sunday.
items.impact: Reid added that they wanted to give Delane some more time to heal if possible. His status will be worth monitoring in practice this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jadarian Price suffers shoulder injury Sunday
items.desc: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury in Sunday's win against the Cardinals.
items.impact: It was originally reported to be a chest injury for Price, but Macdonald said Monday it was a shoulder injury. He  said "it's intact and nothing serious, it seems like." Emmanuel Wilson wound up seeing 21 carries. He would figure to see a big role in Week 3 against the Commanders if Price is sidelined.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) undergoing tests
items.desc: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said RB Jonathon Brooks is undergoing tests on his groin injury.
items.impact: The team is still gathering information on the severity of the injury. There should be an update on Brooks this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) uncertain for Week 3
items.desc: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans did not have an update on Nico Collins' hamstring injury.
items.impact: Wilson noted that according to a source, Collins is currently not expected to play in Week 3 against the Colts. If he remains sidelined, Dalton Schultz will remain a TE1 with Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel also all seeing expanded roles.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) avoids major injury
items.desc: J.K. Dobbins is reportedly "good" after injuring his hamstring in Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.impact: Dobbins was unable to finish Sunday's win over Jacksonville. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week. Rookie RB Jonah Coleman took over the backfield to finish Sunday's game RJ Harvey (hamstring) sidelined.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Drew Lock leans on JSN in win over Cardinals
items.desc: Drew Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals.
items.impact: 155 of his passing yards and all of his touchdowns went to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock was thrust into the starting role because of Sam Darnold's injury, but through most of two weeks, he's been just fine and has leaned on his superstar wideout to do most of the work for him. If he starts again, he gets a nice matchup against the Commanders' struggling defense.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has hat trick of touchdowns in win
items.desc: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 of 11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.impact: JSN has been on an absolute tear to start the season, with 277 yards through the first two games. He's looking QB-proof at the moment, and as long as Drew Lock can continue to get him the ball with Sam Darnold still out, JSN is an auto start. Not that you were sitting him anyway. He gets a great matchup against the Commanders next week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Caleb Williams (hamstring) labeled week-to-week with hamstring injury
items.desc: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is "week-to-week", per HC Ben Johnson. Initial optimism about his status has given way to reality, and it now seems likely Williams will miss time.
items.impact: It's a bummer for Williams, who looked to be on his way to a great start to the year. Tyson Bagent is the next man up in Chicago, and he's shown promise in previous outings when taking over for Williams.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Colts D/ST struggles in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: The Colts' D/ST logged two sacks and allowed 33 points in Sunday night's overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Indianapolis' defense looked bad for a second-straight week on Sunday night. They weren't able to force a single turnover against the Chiefs and ended up allowing 33 points over the course of the night, which was enough to give Kansas City the win in overtime. This unit should not be played in most fantasy leagues for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Spencer Shrader perfect in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: Spencer Shrader went 3-for-3 on his field-goal attempts and 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Shrader did his job on Sunday night. He made all six of his kicks against the Chiefs, which left him with 12 points over the course of the night. That wasn't enough for Indianapolis to pick up the win in overtime, however, as they now drop to 0-2 on the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Laquon Treadwell racks up 61 yards Sunday
items.desc: Laquon Treadwell caught three passes for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The veteran stepped up on Sunday after Alec Pierce left the game due to a heel injury. Treadwell played well and racked up 61 yards on the night, though he still wasn't great from a fantasy perspective. He should be more involved moving forward but still shouldn't be rostered in most league formats.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Avonte Maddox (foot) out for season with foot injury
items.desc: Avonte Maddox (foot) will require season-ending foot surgery to repair the injury he sustained against the Bills on Thursday.
items.impact: It's a tough break for Maddox and the Detroit defense, who lose yet another veteran in what is already a struggling defense. They'll have to bring in some new names and hope for the best in their defensive backfield.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keenan Allen held to one catch Sunday
items.desc: Keenan Allen caught 1-of-5 targets for just five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The veteran saw five opportunities on Sunday night, but he was only able to haul in one catch for five yards over the course of the night. He hasn't looked very good over the first two games of the season, which mitigates a lot of the optimism surrounding him now that Alec Pierce (heel) seems set to miss time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Josh Downs leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Josh Downs hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 72 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The Colts needed Downs to step up on Sunday night, and he did just that, delivering a team-high 72 yards in a narrow loss to the Chiefs. He seems primed to improve as a fantasy option in the near future with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time after aggravating an injury.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyler Warren hauls in touchdown Sunday
items.desc: Tyler Warren hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The young tight end had an up-and-down night on Sunday. On one hand, he finished with a touchdown and six catches on the night, which led to good results in PPR leagues. On the other hand, he only totaled 21 yards on his seven targets, which is poor as far as efficiency goes. Fantasy managers should continue to expect high volume from him moving forward, especially with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Daniel Jones solid in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-31 passing attempts for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Jones didn't have a spectacular showing on Sunday night, but he was pretty solid and limited mistakes for Indianapolis' offense. That was almost enough for them to pick up a road win over Kansas City, but they ended up narrowly losing in overtime. The veteran quarterback shouldn't be rostered in most league formats at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jonathan Taylor scores twice in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: Jonathan Taylor rushed the ball 24 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding four receptions for 40 yards through the air in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Taylor was the engine for Indianapolis' offense on Sunday night. He totaled 132 yards over the course of the night and was able to score two touchdowns on the ground. He has been very strong to start the season and should continue to be considered an elite fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chiefs D/ST struggles in win Sunday
items.desc: The Chiefs' D/ST logged one interception and allowed 30 points in Sunday night's overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Kansas City's defense didn't look good on Sunday night. They allowed Indianapolis to put up 30 points, and they weren't able to log a single sack or turnover beyond one interception. This unit should bounce back and look great in matchups against the Dolphins and Raiders over the next two weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Harrison Butker scores 15 points in OT win Sunday
items.desc: Harrison Butker went 4-for-5 on his field-goal attempts and 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Butker missed one field goal on Sunday night, but outside of that, he was perfect. He made all seven of his other kicks, including a walk-off kick which secured the win for Kansas City in overtime. He should continue to be a good fantasy asset moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cyrus Allen entirely uninvolved Sunday
items.desc: Cyrus Allen didn't see a target or touch in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: The rookie saw very little involvement for a second-straight game on Sunday night, which makes him unlikely to be productive for the foreseeable future. Fantasy managers should feel comfortable dropping him in favor of someone who has been getting more work for the first couple games of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyquan Thornton productive in OT win Sunday
items.desc: Tyquan Thornton caught four passes for 86 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Thornton looked great on Sunday night, leading Kansas City's wideouts with 86 yards on four catches. His production as a downfield threat helped lead the Chiefs to a close overtime win over the Colts, although for fantasy purposes he doesn't project to be of much use for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Xavier Worthy finds end zone in overtime win Sunday
items.desc: Xavier Worthy caught 5-of-7 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Worthy saw good involvement with seven targets on Sunday night, although he was only able to turn that into five catches for 25 yards against the Colts. He was able to score on one of those catches, however, which salvaged his night from a fantasy perspective. He should not be considered a strong option at the wide receiver position until we see some more consistent production from him.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Travis Kelce dominant in overtime win Sunday
items.desc: Travis Kelce hauled in 9-of-11 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Kelce looked great on Sunday night. He led the team in receptions and racked up 101 receiving yards on the night, a number which he failed to hit at all last season. His touchdown was the cherry on top for fantasy managers, and he will likely continue to have good week-to-week value if Patrick Mahomes and KC's offense continues to look this good moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rashee Rice logs 83 yards in win Sunday
items.desc: Rashee Rice caught 4-of-6 targets for 83 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 OT win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Rice was able to bounce back a little bit in Week 2 after a very underwhelming performance to start the season last week. He was able to rack up 83 yards over the course of the night, but he didn't get into the end zone at all, which left him with a mediocre fantasy total. This was a better performance for him, but he was still fourth on the team in terms of targets in this matchup, so fantasy managers should continue to pay attention to his production over the next week or two to see how valuable he will be season-long.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kenneth Walker III totals 178 yards in OT win Sunday
items.desc: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 24 times for 117 yards and caught 6-of-10 targets for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Walker's hot start to the season continued on Sunday night. He totaled 178 yards from scrimmage in a big win over the Colts, and he was able to do that while maintaining terrific efficiency. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy asset for as long as he remains healthy and on the field moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Patrick Mahomes II tosses three touchdowns Sunday
items.desc: Patrick Mahomes II completed 32-of-47 passing attempts for 382 yards and three touchdowns while adding 17 yards on the ground in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Mahomes had an electric game on Sunday night, throwing three touchdowns and totaling nearly 400 yards en route to a narrow win over the Colts. He has been terrific since his return from injury and should be considered a worthwhile starter with week-to-week upside on any given week.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: George Kittle finds the end zone in Week 2
items.desc: George Kittle secured all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: With his Achilles injury further behind him, Kittle's playmaking ability was on display Sunday. The veteran TE led the 49ers in receiving yards and had the longest gain of the day with a 40-yard pickup. Kittle also scored his first touchdown of the campaign on a 12-yard pass from Brock Purdy early in the third quarter. As long as he's healthy, Kittle is among the top TEs in the league.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Demarcus Robinson comes up with three catches in Sunday's win
items.desc: Demarcus Robinson caught all three of his targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Robinson has been targeted three times in each of the first two games of the season, hauling in five of them for 83 yards and a touchdown. He's likely to remain a lower-volume, big-play threat for QB Brock Purdy, but Robinson has been efficient with his looks to this point.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Deebo Samuel Sr. finished with three receptions in Week 2
items.desc: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 31 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Samuel fell well short of the 60 total yards and a touchdown he contributed in Week 1, but he was still significantly involved in Week 2. That should remain the case as long as the veteran playmaker is healthy. Samuel has secured 9-of-11 targets for 79 yards through two games. He's also carried the ball once in each contest, gaining 16 yards.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Mike Evans catches three passes in Week 2 win
items.desc: Mike Evans came down with all three of his targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Evans gained half of his yards in Sunday's win on one catch, as he was limited overall in volume of targets due to Brock Purdy efficiently spreading the ball around. At this point in his career, Evans is not the top-tier WR he once was, but he is showing immediate rapport with Purdy. Evans has hauled in 9-of-10 targets for 103 yards and a score through two games.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Kyle Juszczyk hits paydirt in Week 2 win
items.desc: Kyle Juszczyk secured both of his targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Juszczyk did his thing for the 49ers in Sunday's blowout of the Dolphins. The 10-time Pro Bowl selection scored on a six-yard touchdown strike in the third quarter and gained 21 yards on another catch. He remains a pivotal role player for QB Brock Purdy and the 49ers' offense, but Juszczyk does not get nearly enough touches to make him a fantasy options in the vast majority of leagues.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Kaelon Black gets seven carries in Week 2
items.desc: Kaelon Black gained 25 yards on seven carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: After gaining 65 yards on 14 carries in Week 1, Black saw his attempts cut in half in Week 2. The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Sunday's win, but Brock Purdy more than made up for that with his passing prowess. Black has gained 90 yards on 21 carries through two games, and he maintains decent fantasy value as the backup to Christian McCaffrey.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
items.desc: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Brock Purdy turns in tremendous effort against Dolphins
items.desc: Brock Purdy connected on 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on three carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Purdy is off to an outstanding start this season, and he could hardly have been more prolific in Sunday's rout of the Dolphins. The fifth-year QB has completed a ridiculous 80.4% of his passes so far, averaging 246 yards with a 5-1 TD/INT ratio through two games. Purdy has also rushed for 59 yards on eight carries, including a two-yard scoring scramble on Sunday. He'll be a QB to start against the Cardinals in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jets D/ST registers three sacks in Week 2
items.desc: The Jets D/ST registered three sacks while also forcing one turnover (one fumble recovery) in a 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit was mostly solid outside of a fourth quarter letdown for head coach Aaron Glenn, allowing under 200 offensive yards in a losing effort. The defense will be difficult to trust against a high-powered Detroit Lions offense in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jason Sanders picks up five points in Week 2
items.desc: Jason Sanders converted his lone field goal attempts as well as both of his extra point attempts to finish with five points on the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: Sanders continues a solid start to the season, finishing with five or more points in each of the first two contests. The kicker will look for another steady performance against the Detroit Lions in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Packers D/ST picks up four sacks in Week 2 win
items.desc: The Packers D/ST recorded four sacks in a 20-17 win over the New York Jets in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit made stops when it mattered to carry an inconsistent Green Bay offense, allowing 285 offensive yards in the win. The defense will look to take advantage of an underwhelming Atlanta Falcons offense in Week 3.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Eddy Pineiro makes five PATs in Sunday's win
items.desc: Eddy Pineiro did not attempt a field goal but made all five of his PATs in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: The 49ers found the end zone with each of their first five drives Sunday afternoon, and did not give Pineiro any field-goal chances. That's obviously not going to be the case each week. The veteran should be a solid fantasy option for a squad that looks really strong so far.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Trey Smack picks up eight points in Week 2
items.desc: Trey Smack converted each of his two field goal attempts as well as both of his extra point attempts to finish with eight points in the Packers' 20-17 win over the New York Jets in Week 2.
items.impact: Smack continues a strong start to the season, racking up eight or more points in each of the first two games. The kicker will look for more success in a favorable Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: 49ers D/ST records four sacks, stifles Dolphins offense
items.desc: The 49ers' defense allowed just 13 points on 284 yards of offense while recording four sacks in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: For the second straight week, the 49ers' defense dominated. The unit has surrendered just 20 points in two games, holding both the Rams and Dolphins under 300 yards of total offense. The 49ers will remain a popular play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Vikings D/ST disruptive in Week 2
items.desc: The Vikings D/ST registered four sacks while also forcing two turnovers (one interception, one fumble recovery) in a 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit was able to stand tall against a Chicago ground attack, holding both D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to less than 50 yards rushing each. The defense will look to take advantage of a turnover-prone Tampa Bay Buccaneers offense in Week 3.
